data.name: Slade
data.gender_notes: Slade is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word 'slad,' meaning 'valley,' and 'de,' meaning 'of.' This name may have originated from the valley of Slough or Slaughter, where a significant battle may have taken place. The name Slade carries the meaning “Valley of Slaughter” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Slade usually hope their child will grow to embody valley of slaughter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder to face challenges with courage and faith.
data.etymology: Slade belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Valley of Slaughter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Slade total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.
